name: Ak-Sai Glacier
near: Kashka-Suu — about 20 km as the crow flies (OSM marker). The real starting point is the Ala-Archa alpine camp (~12 km above the park checkpoint), from where it is ~6–7 km on foot via the Racek Hut to the edge of the glacier.
elev: The lower part of the glacier is about 3,300–3,500 m (at the Racek Hut ~3,300–3,400 m; Trip to Kyrgyzstan/Baibol give 3,500 m), the upper reaches are under the crest of the Ak-Sai spur at 4,700–4,875 m (Semenov-Tian-Shansky Peak 4,875 m, Korona 4,860 m, Svobodnaya Koreya 4,740 m).
short: Ak-Sai is the largest glacier of the Ala-Archa gorge, about 5 km long, with a huge icefall; it descends to the Racek Hut from the crest of the highest peaks of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too.
desc: The Ak-Sai Glacier lies at the head of the side gorge of the same name in the Ala-Archa nature park, ~40 km from Bishkek. It is about 5 km long (Baibol Travel), with a huge icefall in the middle section. The glacier flows down from the Ak-Sai spur, where the highest points of the Kyrgyz range rise: Semenov-Tian-Shansky Peak (4,875 m), Korona (4,860 m), Svobodnaya Koreya (4,740 m), Baylyan-Bashi (4,700 m), Simagin (4,400 m) and Boks (4,240 m). At the foot are several climbers’ bases, the best known of which is the Racek Hut; about 80 climbing routes have been laid out on the slopes around. Tourists usually look at the glacier from the moraine by the hut; going onto the ice itself is already a mountaineering task.
guide: The Ak-Sai Glacier is the “stage” for Korona Peak: the best view opens from the moraine right above the Racek Hut, which is reached by a hard but non-technical day hike from the alpine camp. Look closely at the icefall in the middle section — it is the approach to the walls of Korona and Svobodnaya Koreya, where generations of climbers have trained in Ala-Archa. Do not go onto the ice without a rope and skills: crevasses are covered by snow even in summer. If you want to touch the glacier safely, stay overnight at the hut and go with an Ak-Sai Travel guide.
see: The icefall in the middle section of the glacier, a view of Korona, Svobodnaya Koreya and Semenov-Tian-Shansky peaks from the moraine by the Racek Hut; on the way — the Ak-Sai waterfall and the Tepshe plateau; nearby — the Uchitel glacier and lake.
skip: You expect to reach the ice light in half a day — it is 6–7 km and +1,300 m from the alpine camp to the edge of the glacier. You do not tolerate altitude of 3,300+ m. You want to “walk on the glacier” without mountaineering gear and a guide — that is dangerous because of hidden crevasses.
diff: To the edge of the glacier (the moraine by the Racek Hut): a hard non-technical trek of 6–7 km and +1,100–1,350 m one way. Going onto the glacier and climbs are at mountaineering level (crampons, ice axe, rope team, belaying skills); Uchitel Peak is grade 1B, Korona and Svobodnaya Koreya are difficult routes.
when: Late June — September for the trek to the hut and moraine; for climbs — July–August. In winter the glacier and approaches are under avalanche threat; the hut is open year-round, but in winter experience is needed.
hours: No time limits: a natural area within the Ala-Archa park (the checkpoint is open daily). The Racek Hut at the glacier operates year-round (Ak-Sai Travel).
daytime: Morning: the view of the icefall and Korona is best before noon; after lunch there is often cloud and thunderstorms. Set off from the alpine camp before 8:00.
how: Bishkek → Ala-Archa park checkpoint (bus No. 1 from Usubaliev Sq., 50/40 som, or a taxi) → free electric bus ~12 km to the alpine camp → on foot along the Ak-Sai gorge past the waterfall to the Racek Hut (5.7–6 km) → the moraine and the edge of the glacier next to the hut.
needcar: To the park checkpoint — bus No. 1 or a taxi; inside — a free electric bus to the alpine camp (combustion-engine cars have not been allowed in since 01.05.2025); beyond that only on foot.
self: To the moraine by the Racek Hut — yes, if you are fit. Onto the glacier itself — only with mountaineering experience or a guide (Ak-Sai Travel and others).
roadtype: Paved up to the checkpoint and then a road for electric buses to the alpine camp; above — a mountain trail, above the Ak-Sai waterfall steep scree and moraine; on the glacier — ice, snow and crevasses.
traveltime: Bishkek → checkpoint 45–60 min; electric bus to the alpine camp; alpine camp → Racek Hut 4–6 h up, 3–4 h down (ilovekg). As a day hike — 8–11 h; better with an overnight at the hut.
stay: Racek Hut (Ak-Sai Travel): bunk $15 per person, VIP $25, your own tent $3 per person per day; the Light House hut is nearby (ak-sai.com, 2026). Lower down — cottages and yurts at the Ala-Archa alpine camp.
net: There is no mobile network on the route to the hut and at the glacier (asiamixtravel) — offline maps are essential. A signal is available around the checkpoint/alpine camp.
entry: Entry to the Ala-Archa park from 11.06.2026: 250 som for adults, 180 som for children aged 7–14 (24.kg; group 6 data). There is no separate fee for the glacier; an overnight at the hut is at Ak-Sai Travel rates.
transfer: Bus No. 1 — 50/40 som; electric bus — free; taxi Bishkek — checkpoint ~$12–18, private transfer $40–90 (kgnomad 2026).
bring: Trekking boots, poles, a waterproof shell and a warm layer, hat and gloves, 1.5–2 l of water, category 3–4 sunglasses and SPF, a headlamp. For going onto the ice — crampons, ice axe, helmet, harness and rope (only with skills).
warn: The glacier is a mountaineering zone: hidden crevasses, an icefall, rockfall from the moraine. Altitude 3,300+ m — risk of altitude sickness (Emergency Ministry (MChS) evacuations at the Racek Hut in 2026). No phone coverage; in an emergency — 112. Outside summer — avalanches. The glaciers of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too are retreating, moraine edges are unstable.
food: Food at the Racek Hut per the Ak-Sai Travel menu: breakfast $12, lunch $20, dinner $15 (2026); lower down — the cafe at the Ala-Archa alpine camp. There are no local dishes at the glacier — bring a snack and a thermos.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 11 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: a separate “Ak-Sai Glacier” page (d10112272) with reviews; AllTrails: the route to the hut and glacier — 224 reviews. Pros: a real glacier close to the capital, views of Korona. Cons: a hard climb, acclimatisation needed.
photos.0.cap: Svobodnaya Koreya Peak in the Ak-Sai glacier area; not an overview of the whole glacier
p.sum: The edge of the Ak-Sai Glacier is the moraine right by the Racek Hut: the route is the same — bus No. 1 or a taxi to the Ala-Archa checkpoint (entry 250 som), the free electric bus to the alpine camp and 6–9 km on foot with +1,100–1,350 m of climbing. You can look at the glacier from the moraine without equipment. Onto the ice itself — only roped, with crampons, ice axe, helmet and a guide: crevasses and bergschrunds, and routes to the surrounding peaks start at 1B–3A. It is most convenient to spend the night at the Racek Hut ($15 bunk) and head out to the glacier snout and Lake Uchitel early in the morning.

p.apps.0.last: Phone coverage, cafe and toilets — at the checkpoint and alpine camp. Food, sleeping bag and gas — at the Racek Hut (Ak-Sai Travel). ATMs and fuel stations — in Bishkek

The glacier is retreating, moraine edges are unstable. The abnormal heat of summer 2025 changed ice conditions on the slopes of Korona Peak (summitx, 2026)

p.iti.0.title: One day (moraine only)
p.iti.0.plan: Start from the alpine camp before 8:00 → hut by 12:00 → 30–40 min on the moraine with a view of the icefall → descent by 17:00. Hard; better with an overnight
p.iti.1.title: 2 days: hut + glacier
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: climb to the hut, night ($15 + dinner $15). Day 2: at 6:00 head to the glacier snout and Lake Uchitel (2–3 h), breakfast at the hut, descent, evening in Bishkek
p.iti.2.title: Mountaineering option (2–7 days)
p.iti.2.plan: Night at the hut → climb Uchitel (1B) with a guide → with experience — Korona/Svobodnaya Koreya or the weekly Ak-Sai course
p.iti.3.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.3.plan: The Racek Hut (the same spot), Ala-Archa national park (gondola, Ak-Sai waterfall), the Chunkurchak gorge on the next day
p.season: July — August: no snow on the trail, the best windows for climbs, up to +25 °C in the daytime, crowded at the hut, more rockfall and open crevasses on the glacier. September — early October: stable. Mid-October — mid-April: crampons needed on the approach, avalanches; ice climbing. May — June: snowfalls, until 20 June blizzards are possible at the hut (summitx)
p.budget.economy: ≈1,000–2,500 som for a day trip to the moraine (bus, entry 250 som, a snack). With an overnight at the hut — plus ≈$40 (bunk + dinner + breakfast)
p.budget.comfort: A guided one-day tour ≈AU$645 (KG Country); 2 days with the Uchitel climb ≈CA$611; a mountain guide — roughly $80–100/day plus his food and lodging
p.permits: No border-zone permit needed. A ticket to the Ala-Archa park — 250 som (children 180), sold at the checkpoint. In climbing programmes a “permit” is mentioned separately — check the climbing permit with the operator
p.access: Only for prepared adults; not suitable for children, older people or wheelchair users. Onto the glacier itself — only with mountaineering skills
